observations.body: James blesses endurance under trial, says God tempts no one, traces temptation through one’s own desire, and contrasts desire’s path with God’s good gifts and new birth.
observations.label: James separates God from the source of temptation

observations.body: The passage presents Enduring, desiring, conceiving, sinning, and giving birth as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Enduring, desiring, conceiving, sinning, and giving birth

observations.body: The passage places God gives good gifts and tempts no one beside Enduring, desiring, conceiving, sinning, and giving birth.
observations.label: God gives good gifts and tempts no one

payload.posture: Read James 1:12–18 as one movement in the temptation of Jesus, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: Crown of life, death, and first fruits
payload.title: James separates God from the source of temptation
